verdict.rationale: Kong's AI Gateway and Catalog reference MCP servers as first-class entities it can register, govern, and route traffic to/from (e.g. Catalog inventories 'MCP servers', AI Gateway provides 'MCP traffic governance, MCP security and MCP observability'), implying Kong can plug in existing MCP servers so their tools flow through its infrastructure. However, most concrete MCP evidence is about Kong auto-generating/exposing its own MCP servers from REST APIs rather than consuming external MCP servers as a client, so the 'use their tools' framing is only indirectly supported. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of Kong connecting to arbitrary third-party MCP servers as a client and invoking their tools, and independent/hands-on confirmation of this workflow.
